title: What a Pass and Trip Protection Plan Has Paid Out and the Credit Issued on a Granite Ridge Season Pass
content:
Where the household holds a Pass and Trip Protection plan written over a season pass on the account, a share of what that plan has paid out this season is taken off the amount coming back on a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass given up, because the household is not put in funds twice for the same season.

**First.** Where the collective's protection records show a plan written over a season pass on the household account whose claim has been settled, the whole of what that plan has paid out this season is taken off, a share of 100 per cent.

**Second.** Where those records show such a plan with a claim still open, half of what it has paid out is taken off, a share of 50 per cent.

**Otherwise.** In any other case nothing it has paid out is taken off by this rule.

### The plan records this rule reads

The plan is a Pass and Trip Protection record on the same household account whose covered holding is a season pass. Two things are read: the state that plan stands in, and the payouts standing on that household's protection account.

| The plan written over a season pass on the household account | Share of what it has paid out that is taken off |
| --- | --- |
| its claim has been settled | 100 per cent |
| it has a claim still open | 50 per cent |
| it stands in force with no claim | none by this rule |
| no such plan on the account | none by this rule |

### Worked on a hypothetical account

A household whose Pass and Trip Protection plan over a Granite Ridge Summit Plus Pass shows payouts of 620.00 this season.

Where the claim on that plan has been settled, the whole 620.00 is taken off the amount coming back. Where the claim is still open, half of it is taken off, which is 310.00. Where the plan stands in force with no claim on it, nothing it has paid out is taken off by this rule.
